benchmark.hardware: Apple M3 Pro, 36 GB unified memory
benchmark.frame_count_note: The MP4 header reports 298 frames, but FFmpeg and OpenCV both decode 286. Throughput uses the 286 frames the analysis processed.
benchmark.result_check: All three runs produced the same shot result: release at 6.79 s, made at frame 243, shot-space score 97.9.

charts.title: Frame-processing throughput
charts.y_label: Decoded frames per processing second (higher is better)

charts.title: Cumulative ball detection work
charts.y_label: Seconds across detector calls (lower is better)
charts.timing_scope: Includes detector preprocessing, ONNX execution, decoding, and readback. The same 286 full-frame and 134 side-crop calls were made in each serial run.

display_notes: These are single-run measurements on one clip, not averages or a general benchmark across videos.
The throughput chart measures offline processing speed, not the source video's 29.77 FPS playback rate.
Ball and pose work can overlap in the two-frame pipeline. Do not stack their summed times or compare the overlapped ball-work total with serial call latency.
The Core ML configuration requests CPU and Neural Engine execution; it does not establish the exact hardware used for every model operation.
